the high-temperature cellulose-rich sediment and water column at Great Boiling Spring is a natural hotbed for cellulose-degrading microorganisms and provides an ideal environment for in situ cellulose enrichment.

the microbial communities that were found in the enrichments were similar in composition to the natural microbial communities, and that these communities were dominated by cellulolytic and fermenting bacteria and archaea.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-temperature cellulose-degrading communities are highly enriched in the Great Boiling Spring sediment and water column and are dominated by phylotype groups known to be cellulolytic and/or hemicellulotic in pure culture.
the high-temperature cellulose-degrading microbial community in Great Boiling Springs is dominated by known thermophilic species and that a substantial portion may be represented in pure culture.
